pending_commit.commit_message: BACKPORT: Add udmabuf misc device A driver to let userspace turn memfd regions into dma-bufs. Use case: Allows qemu create dmabufs for the vga framebuffer or virtio-gpu ressources. Then they can be passed around to display those guest things on the host. To spice client for classic full framebuffer display, and hopefully some day to wayland server for seamless guest window display. qemu test branch: https://git.kraxel.org/cgit/qemu/log/?h=sirius/udmabuf Cc: David Airlie <airlied@linux.ie> Cc: Tomeu Vizoso <tomeu.vizoso@collabora.com> Cc: Laurent Pinchart <laurent.pinchart@ideasonboard.com> Cc: Daniel Vetter <daniel@ffwll.ch> Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com> Acked-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch> Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20180827093444.23623-1-kraxel@redhat.com (cherry picked from commit fbb0de795078190a9834b3409e4b009cfb18a6d4) Signed-off-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Backport notes: The following upstream commits refactored some code, and were changed back locally: f9b67f ("dma-buf: Rename dma-ops to prevent conflict with kunmap_atomic") Changed {.kmap, .kunmap} to {.map, .unmap} in struct dma_buf_ops. 11bac8 ("mm, fs: reduce fault, page_mkwrite, and pfn_mkwrite to take only vmf") Stopped passing struct vm_area_struct *vma into the page fault handler. 5aadc4 ("shmem: rename functions that are memfd-related") Changed shmem_fcntl(..) into memfd_fcntl(..). BUG=chromium:892806 TEST=compiles Change-Id: I532b74a5aadcce2b74b70d42b01568a5a9979fd6 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1265395 Tested-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Robert Tarasov <tutankhamen@chromium.org>

CRAS: hfp_slc - Fix codec negotiation We're seeing peripheral not sending reply to +BCS command until specific other AT command is sent and handled. To make sure codec negotiation is reliable, check and resend +BCS command after any other AT command is handled. This patch also increase the timeout to 500ms for when SLC established until codec negotiation is completed. This helps to ensure codec negotiation has completed when BT audio option becomes available to user. And it only affects the case when codec negotiation never completes(for whatever reason) by introducing delay to when user sees BT audio option show up on UI. hwid: Remove chassis from default encoding and increase RO EC field length The 'chassis' was introduced after Reef (multi-OEM zerg) and before Unibuild (Coral). It had few assumptions that are no longer true today, for example: - `chassis` was designed to support multiple projects (zerg or WL) in a single HWID database file, but follower units are now always identified as new 'model' today which has its own HWID database file. - Since Unibuild, the 'chassis' is always reported as model name. - Since Unibuild, white label units share same chassis name. So what it served was replaced by either model name or SKU information. Given all newer projects will only do Unibuild, we should release the 5 bits for better usage. In the meantime, we previously allocated 3 bits for AP RO firmware, and 2 for EC RO. These were not sufficient because devices may have 2~3 unsupported RO (EVT, DVT, PVT) and 2~3 times of refresh, so in the end we often see devices increasing fields for these, making it harder to search and maintain, for example counting EC RO field length: nocturne(3), shyvana(3), grabbiter(3), sand(6), apel(3), eve(6), atlas(6), dumo(4), robo(4), wukong(7), ..... So let's try to make it default to 5 bits now. Note that dram, ap/ec RO fw version and fw key fields have moved to different location. Devices with existing HWID database file do not need to change anything. This is simply changing the default new file created by HWID database builder. BUG=None TEST=make test Change-Id: Ic297463ea739531edc60164fa6ead47da266921a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1732612 Tested-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org>

dlcservice: Install completion determined from DBus signal When update_engine signals its listeners of a status update, dlcservice is one of those listeners. Previously, dlcservice determined that update engine was done installing DLC(s) based off that fact that dlcservice held onto the DLC(s) it sent over to update_engine and that update_engine sent a status with operation IDLE. Now, a more solidified method of letting update_engine, who knows whether an install or update is in progress, indicate this field through `is_install` within |update_engine::StatusResult| is used by dlcservice to determined an install completion.
